system.description:
No one is entirely certain how the Drek came to be. Some suggest they were magical experiments that were loosed into the wild in some forgotten epoch. Whatever the case may be, they exist, and are known to have killed their gods in a distant war that wiped out two of their ancient bloodlines. In various oral traditions, their gods pressed them to war and paid the price when the drek realized they had been fooled. In others, they simply turned on their gods for being a nuisance

A vaguely reptillian and strangely feline being, drek combine the worst traits of both groups into an unharmonious whole. Their faces are not unlike a cat’s with a broad but flat nose and large searching eyes showing slit pupils. Their mouths are crammed with the teeth of a crocodile, and they often bear fins or ridges that look aquatic in origin. Lithoderms mar their shoulders and arms in a manner reminiscent of scales, and their powerful, clublike, tails force them into the hunched posture of a predator. Yet they bear hair in just as many cases as fins, and sideburns that sometimes connect across the chin into dark, bristly manes are not uncommon either.

The drek are a fairly aggressive people, though they are not wicked or hostile by nature. They are driven and direct; blunt in many ways. They tend to grow in warhordling cultures more than any other, but are known in nearly any society in some number.

Drek Traits

Type: Humanoid

Age: Drek grow swiftly, reaching their full height by 7 years of age, but continue to develop their physical and mental characteristics until they are roughly 20 years of age. This can become quite painful in their teen years when their adult teeth come in, and their jaw and lower skull adapt to the new, longer, teeth.

Size: Medium. The overall body length, including tail, of a drek is usually 7-8ft, though their hunched posture gives them a ‘height’ of 5’8” on average.

Speed: 35ft. While the Drek sometimes appear to have an ungainly gait, they are quite swift.

Vision: Darkvision 60ft. Drek darkvision relies on the tapetum lucidum, which causes their eyes to glow in dim but not pitch black conditions, and a form of movement based impressions, causing drek in pitch black conditions to move their heads from side to side.

Regeneration: Wounded beasts don’t live long on death planets. Once per long rest, a drek can expend a hit die as a bonus action to recover HP. When you do so, you may reattach a missing body part as per the Regenerate spell.

Tail Strike: As a bonus action, you can use your tail to strike nearby targets. This natural weapon uses your Strength modifier to attack and deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage with no modifier.

Drek Gifts

While all the drek were created at the same time, their people were spread across a variety of different habitats and biomes and they evolved to have some traits which are somewhat unique to a given bloodline.

Jungle (Tookreh Bloodline)

The darkened jungles are inhabited by predators of every possible description. Even the plantlife is occasionally murderous and relies on dead animal matter to ensure the soil near their roots is filled with nutrients. Thus, the drek of the jungle rely on keen senses and a resistance to plant toxins to survive.

Ambush Predator: You gain proficiency in the Perception and Stealth skills.

Swift Climber: You gain a climb speed of 30ft and gain expertise on checks made to climb.

Toxin Resistance: You have resistance to poison damage and immunity to ingested poisons and toxins.

Saltwater (Otanreh Bloodline)

Living in the shallow reaches of oceans is a fair trade off for most species. You can’t grow quite as large as the monsters of the deepwater, but there’s plenty of life near to the shoreline to consume. For Saltwater adapted drek, this meant wading through the shallows, swimming with shark-like creatures offshore, and retreating to land to sleep.

Fast Swimmer: You gain a swim speed of 30ft, and you gain expertise on checks made to swim.

Deep Breaths: You can hold your breath for up to 30 minutes.

Slippery when Wet: Your people had to avoid being consumed by bigger beasts, granting you expertise on checks made to escape or maintain a grapple.

Savannah (Adareh Bloodline)

Holding to ancestral memories of golden savannahs shining red under a sunset, the drek who evolved in savannahs combined a variety of tactics to capture prey and escape from other predators; techniques now written in the DNA of their descendants.

Lope: Your speed increases by +5ft.

Persistence: You require only 4 hours of rest to complete a long rest and may be active for 18 hours a day without incurring fatigue.

Pounce: You can use a bonus action to make a leap without provoking opportunity attacks. The distance of the leap is 5ft per point of proficiency bonus.

You may use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier and recover expended uses on a long rest.

Drek Paragon Traits

At 10th level, you gain an additional trait from your heritage chosen from the list below.

Lunging Strikes

You are able to use your hunched position and the heavy counterweight of your tail to extend your reach with melee weapons by 5ft. In addition, your swim or climb speed, if you have one, increases by 10ft. You can now recover 2 uses of Pounce on a short rest if you possess the ability.

Lick Wounds

When you use your regeneration heritage trait, you can now expend up to three hit dice.
